summary: Customer requests tenant-id hash mapping + timezone-normalized audit bundle with X.509 signing chain for quarterly SOC2 evidence
description:
Issue summary:
FinGrid Capital (enterprise) has requested an on-demand quarterly audit bundle with the following constraints:
  1) Tenant identifiers must be delivered as irreversible SHA-256 salted hashes with a per-tenant salt provided by FinGrid (mapping file must be delivered separately and encrypted).
  2) All event timestamps must be normalized to the customer's preferred timezone (America/New_York) and include original UTC timestamp as an additional field.
  3) The entire bundle must be cryptographically signed using an X.509 certificate chain issued by Redwood's signing service; customer requires the full chain plus OCSP stapling proof where possible.
  4) PIi redaction: username/email fields should be pseudonymized according to agreed field map; redaction must be reversible only via the encrypted mapping file delivered to the customer via SFTP.
 5) Delivery format: compressed Parquet files partitioned by date and event_type, with a manifest CSV that includes checksums (sha256) for each file.
Impact:
FinGrid needs this bundle to complete SOC2 quarterly evidence collection; delay blocks their compliance attestation. Customer flagged potential contract penalty if not delivered within contract window (end of quarter).
Requested deliverables (customer-provided):
  - Per-tenant salt file (FinGrid will upload to our secure intake bucket).
  - Desired timezone string (America/New_York).
  - Pseudonymization field map (CSV).
Environment:
  - Production audit stream for FinGrid workspace id: fg-8482
  - Regions: primary us-east, replica eu-west
Steps taken so far:
  - Support confirmed requirements and escalation to Engineering (this ticket).
  - SRE validated that historical audit retention covers requested quarter; export tooling can produce Parquet + manifest.
  - Signing team confirmed X.509 chain support exists but OCSP stapling requires additional config and test vectors from customer CA.
Open questions / blockers:
  - Does FinGrid require HSM-backed signing for the delivered bundle, or will Redwood-signed chain be sufficient? (Customer later clarified Redwood-signed is acceptable if chain and OCSP proof are provided.)
  - Is the per-tenant salt rotation acceptable if we store the salt for future replays? Customer requested we do not retain the plaintext mapping beyond delivery window.
Acceptance criteria:
  - Audit bundle SFTP delivery completed to FinGrid staging box with manifest and checksums.
  - Files signed with X.509 chain and OCSP responses attached; signature verification steps documented in delivery note.
  - Hash mapping file encrypted with customer's public key and uploaded separately; Redwood does not retain plaintext mapping beyond delivery confirmation.
  - Timestamps normalized to America/New_York with original_utc_ts included for every event.
  - Customer confirms receipt and successful verification within SLA window.
Logs / links for engineers:
  - Export job id: export-fg-202603-Q1
  - Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/internal/dashboards/audit-exports?job=export-fg-202603-Q1
  - Signing service runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/Signing+Service+Runbook
Deployment notes / timeline:
  - Target: deliver by 2026-03-15 per SLA.
  - Work plan: engineering to produce export -> signing -> create manifest -> SFTP upload -> customer verification.
  - If OCSP stapling tests fail, fallback: include stamped OCSP responses from our OCSP responder and document validation steps.
